items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative Zero for Order Greater than Degree
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (p : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ), p.natDegree < n → (Polynomial.hasseDeriv n) p = 0
items.informal_description: If the natural degree of a polynomial $ p $ is less than $ n $, then the $ n $-th Hasse derivative of $ p $ is the zero polynomial, i.e., $ \text{hasseDeriv}^n(p) = 0 $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Monomial in Polynomial Ring
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k n : ℕ) (r : R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) ((Polynomial.monomial n) r) = (Polynomial.monomial (n - k)) (↑(n.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the monomial $ rX^n $ in the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ is given by $ \binom{n}{k} r X^{n - k} $. This expresses how the Hasse derivative acts on monomials by scaling the coefficient by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient Formula for Hasse Derivative of Order k
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ),
  ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f).coeff n = ↑((n + k).choose k) * f.coeff (n + k)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $ n $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of a polynomial $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ is equal to $ \binom{n + k}{k} $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ X^{n + k} $ in $ f $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k Applied to a Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f = f.sum fun i r => (Polynomial.monomial (i - k)) (↑(i.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ and a polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ applied to $ f $ is given by $ D^{(k)}(f) = \sum_{i} \binom{i}{k} \cdot a_i \cdot X^{i - k} $, where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ f $. This expression sums over all monomials in $ f $, scaling each by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{i}{k} $ and reducing the exponent by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k on Polynomial Ring
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → ℕ → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ is an $ R $-linear map $ D^{(k)} : R[X] 	o R[X] $ defined by $ D^{(k)}(a_i X^i) =  inom{i}{k} a_i X^{i - k} $ on monomials and extended linearly. This operation generalizes the usual derivative by scaling each coefficient $ a_i $ by the binomial coefficient $  inom{i}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Zero Product Iff Zero Factor in Finite Support
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {β : Type u_7} [inst : Zero α] [inst_1 : CommMonoidWithZero β] [Nontrivial β]
  [NoZeroDivisors β] {f : ι →₀ α} {g : ι → α → β}, f.prod g = 0 ↔ ∃ i ∈ f.support, g i (f i) = 0
items.informal_description: The product of $ g(a, f(a)) $ over the support of a finite support function $ f : \alpha \to_0 M $ equals zero if and only if there exists an element $ i $ in the support of $ f $ such that $ g(i, f(i)) = 0 $. This equivalence holds in a commutative monoid with zero $ N $, leveraging the finite support property and zero absorption.

items.informal_name: Product Zero iff Factor Zero for Dependent Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u} {γ : Type w} {β : ι → Type v} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → Zero (β i)]
  [inst_2 : CommMonoidWithZero γ] [Nontrivial γ] [NoZeroDivisors γ] [inst_5 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (β i)]
  {f : Π₀ (i : ι), β i} {g : (i : ι) → β i → γ}, f.prod g = 0 ↔ ∃ i ∈ f.support, g i (f i) = 0
items.informal_description: The product of $ g(i, f(i)) $ over the support of a dependent finite support function $ f $ is zero if and only if there exists an index $ i $ in the support of $ f $ such that $ g(i, f(i)) = 0 $. The support of $ f $ is the finite set of indices $ i $ where $ f(i) \neq 0 $.

items.informal_name: Non-Zero Product Criterion for Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {ι : Type u_2} {β : Type u_7} [inst : Zero α] [inst_1 : CommMonoidWithZero β] [Nontrivial β]
  [NoZeroDivisors β] {f : ι →₀ α} {g : ι → α → β}, f.prod g ≠ 0 ↔ ∀ i ∈ f.support, g i (f i) ≠ 0
items.informal_description: The product of $ g(i, f(i)) $ over all $ i $ in the support of a finite support function $ f : \alpha \to_0 M $ is non-zero if and only if every $ g(i, f(i)) $ is non-zero for all $ i $ in the support of $ f $. This holds when $ M $ is a commutative monoid with zero and no zero divisors.

items.informal_name: Non-Zero Product Criterion for Dependent Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u} {γ : Type w} {β : ι → Type v} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → Zero (β i)]
  [inst_2 : CommMonoidWithZero γ] [Nontrivial γ] [NoZeroDivisors γ] [inst_5 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (β i)]
  {f : Π₀ (i : ι), β i} {g : (i : ι) → β i → γ}, f.prod g ≠ 0 ↔ ∀ i ∈ f.support, g i (f i) ≠ 0
items.informal_description: For a dependent finite support function $ f $ from an index type $ \iota $ to a family of types $ \beta(i) $ with zero, and a function $ g $ mapping each index $ i $ and value $ f(i) $ to a commutative monoid with zero and no zero divisors $ \gamma $, the product of $ g(i, f(i)) $ over the support of $ f $ is non-zero if and only if every $ g(i, f(i)) $ is non-zero. This equivalence relies on the absence of zero divisors in $ \gamma $, ensuring that the product cannot vanish unless at least one term does.

items.informal_name: Finite Product Equals Zero When Function Has Zero in Finite Support
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M₀ : Type u_7} [inst : CommMonoidWithZero M₀] (f : α → M₀) (x : α),
  f x = 0 → (Function.mulSupport f).Finite → ∏ᶠ (x : α), f x = 0
items.informal_description: Let $ M $ be a commutative monoid with zero, and let $ f : \alpha \to M $ be a function. If there exists an element $ x \in \alpha $ such that $ f(x) = 0 $, and the multiplicative support of $ f $ (the set of elements $ a \in \alpha $ where $ f(a) \ne 1 $) is finite, then the finite product $ \prod^\mathrm{fin} f $ over $ \alpha $ equals zero.
